metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment alternates frequently (e.g., +1/-1 cycles), model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; reduce forecast volatility in 3-5 day horizons.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3-7 days; apply downward correction of 10-20% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ consecutive days, model tends to underestimate true price (especially in 10-30 day horizons); add 2-5% upward bias to forecast.
- Mean reversion is stronger in 15-30 day horizons when sentiment is neutral or mixed; model often fails to revert; adjust forecast toward 30-day moving average if sentiment is flat.
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 3-5% per day until sentiment shifts or price stabilizes.
- In high-sentiment volatility periods (e.g., +1/-1 alternating), model overestimates 30-day horizon; cap forecast at 1.5x recent 14-day average to avoid overextension.
